resources.string: Uses your chosen Bluetooth hands-free device for call speaker and microphone audio while Android Auto handles everything else.
Your chosen Bluetooth for calls. Android Auto for everything else.
Start by allowing nearby Bluetooth device and phone-account access.
Complete the one-time ADB authorization. Android provides no normal permission dialog for this non-dialer utility.

Select a paired Bluetooth device for call speaker and microphone audio: a headset, earbuds, speakerphone, or car system. It must use classic Bluetooth hands-free (HFP) and appear in your Phone app’s call-audio selector. LE Audio-only devices are not supported yet.
Setup is complete. Enable automatic routing when you are ready.
Automation is enabled. Each cellular call still needs Android Auto, a connected classic hands-free device, and an identifiable call endpoint. VoIP and app-managed calls are not supported.
No completed routing session has been recorded yet.
Target HFP audio confirmed at call start; check the selected speaker and microphone
Target HFP audio takeover observed after initial confirmation
Complete the required setup steps below to enable automation.
Automatic routing is off. You can test once before enabling it.
Automatic routing is on. Safety checks still run for every call.
Not connected — automatic routing will wait
Not detected yet — automatic routing will wait
Needed to identify paired call devices and verify eligible cellular calls.

Bluetooth access lets the app identify your already-paired call device. Phone-account access is used only to verify that a call is cellular and not an emergency call. The app does not read contacts, call history, or audio.
Not authorized. A normal car association cannot grant protected Telecom access.
Choose the preferred Bluetooth call device first.
Authorization is still missing. Check the package name and rerun the command after reinstalling.

Android reserves this access for the default dialer, system apps, and eligible wearable companions. This utility must not replace your Phone app, and a car association is not a valid shortcut.

1. On the phone, enable Developer options and USB debugging.
2. Install Android Platform Tools on the computer.
3. Connect the phone, unlock it, and approve the USB-debugging prompt.
4. Run:

%1$s

5. Return here and tap Verify.

The app will not report success until Android confirms the AppOp. Reinstalling the APK can require this step again.
No device selected. Pair your call device in Android Bluetooth settings first.
While parked, connect both call devices, start a normal non-emergency call, and tap below. The app uses only a current Telecom endpoint and stops if the selected device cannot be identified uniquely.
Not configured — automatic routing has no selector recovery

For recovery from a stuck call selector, choose the exact Bluetooth call device used by the Android Auto head unit. Without it, recovery is unavailable. After a failed one-shot route, the app can restore the call selector only when this device is confirmed to own HFP audio. It never retries the preferred device. Leave this unset if the other call device is uncertain.
Battery settings (only if calls are missed)
Use this only if real tests show missed calls while the phone is idle. A battery exemption does not guarantee Telecom binding, and the app will not change this setting automatically.
Private by design: no internet, audio recording, contacts, or call-log access.
Open-source Android utility for choosing the Bluetooth hands-free endpoint used by eligible calls. Android Auto remains connected for navigation and media.
No app is available to open this link.
Checking the selected device’s call transport…
Choose a call device to check compatibility.
Classic hands-free connection observed. During a call, the device must also appear in the Phone app’s audio selector. This does not verify its speaker or microphone.

LE Audio or hearing-aid connection observed; no classic hands-free connection observed. This transport is not supported yet. Automation waits for classic HFP. If available, enable “Phone calls” for this device in Bluetooth settings.
No call-profile connection observed for the selected device. Connect it and enable “Phone calls” in Bluetooth settings, then refresh.
Call transport could not be fully checked. Connect the selected device, check Bluetooth access, and refresh. Automation still requires fresh HFP evidence during the call.

While parked, test a normal cellular call with Android Auto connected. Check the selected device’s speaker, ask the other person to confirm its microphone, check navigation, and check that media resumes after the call. Keep the phone away from the selected device when checking its microphone. Record only what you observed. These answers are your report, separate from Android’s route evidence.
Did call sound come from the selected Bluetooth device?
Did the other person confirm your voice came through the selected device’s microphone?
Did Android Auto navigation continue working during the call?
Did Android Auto media resume normally after the call?
Observations recorded in the redacted log. Export it with your test report.
Call-device configuration changed. Start a new test report for this setup.
